sections.h2: Maize is cheapest in the central states and dearest in the south

chart.title: Maize, Oct 2026: Madhya Pradesh Rs 131 below all-India, Tamil Nadu Rs 379 above
chart.sub: Agmarknet state price minus the all-India price, October 2026 to the 23rd, Rs/quintal.
ref: 0 = the all-India price, Rs 2,202 a quintal

sections.means: Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan sold maize Rs 119 to Rs 131 below the all-India price in October 2026, while Tamil Nadu paid Rs 379 more.
sections.todo: Buy maize from the central states at the time of their harvest, rather than from the dearer southern markets.

sections.h2: Maize's cheap season moves with each harvest; rice stays in a narrow band

chart.title: Maize's seasonal swing reaches 45% in Punjab; rice's stays at 5–9%
chart.sub: Seasonal swing between the cheapest and dearest month, 2019 to 2025, %.

sections.means: Maize's seasonal price swing is 12% in Uttar Pradesh, 30% in Maharashtra and 45% in Punjab, against 5 to 9% for rice.
sections.todo: Time purchases to each state's cheap month, which runs from Tamil Nadu in January to Punjab and Uttar Pradesh in June and the kharif belt in October.

sections.h2: Holding maize or rice for six months lost money in all 20 state-and-grain pairs

chart.title: Six-month carry lost Rs 135–212 a quintal on average in each maize state
chart.sub: Average six-month carry result after rent, interest and shrinkage, Rs/quintal, tested from January 2023.

sections.means: Across the maize states shown, the average six-month carry result was a loss of Rs 135 to Rs 212 a quintal.
sections.todo: Stockpile only in a genuine glut, when a state's price is 15% or more below its 12-month average.

sections.h2: All-India maize price index ranges from 0.95 in October to 1.04 in August

chart.title: All-India maize: the monthly index peaks at 1.04 in August and bottoms at 0.95 in October
chart.sub: Calendar-month average divided by the average of all months, full years 2019 to 2025 (1.00 = average month).

sections.means: The all-India index is lowest at 0.95 in October, when the monsoon crop arrives, and highest at 1.04 in August, over the 2019 to 2025 full years.
sections.todo: Buy in October and November, when the monsoon crop arrives, rather than storing grain through the year.
